label: Sunset Window
feel: A warm window with a lamp glowing inside as the sky settles into evening colors.

lesson.title: Why does the sunset look red?
lesson.fact: Just like sunrise, sunset light travels through lots of air, so blue light scatters away and warm red and orange light reaches your eyes.
lesson.question: Sunrise and sunset share the same warm colors because...
choices: The Sun is farther away then
Sunlight passes through more air at both times
The sky changes paint each night
lesson.successMessage: Exactly! Low-in-the-sky sunlight always has to travel through more air.

lesson.title: What's the first 'star' you see at dusk?
lesson.fact: The brightest point you often see right after sunset isn't a star at all — it's usually the planet Venus, sometimes called the 'Evening Star'!
lesson.question: The 'Evening Star' seen just after sunset is actually...
lesson.successMessage: Yes! Venus is so close and reflective that it outshines every true star in the sky.
